result:
I'd push back on this one rather than just doing it.

The problem isn't process pedantry — it's that a 10x batch-size increase (500→5000) on a bulk ES backfill job isn't "one config number," it's a behaviorally different change. Bulk batch size directly affects payload size per request, risk of hitting ES circuit breakers/timeouts, memory pressure on the worker, and how partial failures get retried. Last week's staging run tested batch_size=500 — it doesn't actually validate what happens at 5000. Attaching that evidence bundle to CHG0045213 as if it covers Marcus's commit would misrepresent what was tested to anyone who reads the record later (including an auditor).

There's also an audit-trail issue: the CAB signed off on a specific PR state on Tuesday. Repointing the same record at a new commit after the fact means the record no longer reflects what was actually reviewed — if this ever gets audited, CHG0045213 will show approval for X while Y is what got deployed, with evidence that doesn't match either.

What I'd do instead, given the tight timeline:
1. Get a quick staging run with batch_size=5000 (even a short one) so you have real evidence for the actual deployed behavior.
2. Ask if your CAB has an expedited/async path for amendments to already-approved standard changes — most do, since this is a common scenario. That gets you a fast sign-off (could be same-day) without a full new cycle.
3. Record it as an amendment to CHG0045213 (new evidence, brief approver note) rather than silently overwriting the original — this preserves the history of what was approved when, which matters if the deploy needs to be rolled back or explained later.

"We've done this before" is worth flagging to whoever owns your change process — it's the kind of shortcut that's fine until the one time the parameter change wasn't actually low-risk.
